title: Screen Dimmer by Shardapps
shortDescription: A lightweight Windows 11 screen dimmer with a tray slider, monitor and virtual desktop profiles, six themes and optional startup.
description:
Make a bright desktop feel softer with Screen Dimmer by Shardapps, a small, open-source screen dimmer for Windows 11.

Open the compact slider with Alt+S, choose your preferred brightness, and get back to work. Adjust all displays together or select one monitor, and keep independent brightness profiles for Windows virtual desktops. No account is needed, and the app works offline.

USE IT FOR
• A gentler desktop during late-night reading, coding or study.
• External monitors that still look too bright at their lowest hardware setting.
• Matching the perceived brightness of different screens.
• Quickly dimming a workspace, pausing for 15 minutes, or restoring every display.

SMALL CONTROLS, USEFUL OPTIONS
• A compact flyout above the taskbar and a quiet system tray home.
• Screen selection, screen identification and brightness presets.
• Different brightness for work, study and entertainment desktops in Windows Task View.
• Six palettes: Pearl, Midnight, Graphite, Ocean, Forest and Sunset, plus System.
• Smooth brightness changes and short transitions that respect Windows animation settings.
• Optional warm tint, configurable shortcut and adjustment step.
• Opt-in Windows startup, with a separate option to resume saved dimming.
• Immediate emergency restore with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12.

Built with native Windows APIs, without a bundled browser runtime. No advertising, telemetry, screen recording or keystroke recording. Preferences stay on your device.

ALPHA RELEASE
This is an early Microsoft Store alpha. Feedback and reproducible compatibility reports help shape the next release. The source and issue tracker are available at https://github.com/shardapps/screen.

Screen Dimmer changes perceived brightness through software. It does not change a monitor's physical backlight or promise battery savings. Uniform all-display dimming uses Windows desktop color processing; separate monitor levels use compatibility overlays with narrower full-screen coverage. HDR, protected video, remote sessions and true exclusive full-screen games vary by environment. Windows sign-in, lock and UAC secure screens are outside the app's scope.

Works on Windows 11 desktop PCs, with x64 and ARM64 packages.
releaseNotes: Alpha 2 — adds opt-in brightness profiles for named Windows virtual desktops, including separate monitor levels. Fixes the blank display picker before hover, refines all six themes and native controls, clarifies startup/resume options, and improves brightness/flyout pacing with animation-only timers. Keeps the native lightweight design and adds same-host memory regression checks.
features: Compact brightness slider with Alt+S access and system tray controls
Independent brightness for physical monitors and Windows virtual desktop profiles
Six refined themes plus System, with Windows high-contrast priority
Smooth transitions that respect Windows animation preferences
Brightness presets, optional warm tint and a 15-minute pause
Opt-in Windows startup and separate saved-dimming resume
Configurable opening shortcut and adjustment step
Offline and open source, with no ads, account or telemetry

certificationNotes: Native C++20 Win32 utility. No login or test account is required. Starts paused by default; move the slider to enable dimming. Alt+S opens the flyout; a settings icon opens Displays, Appearance and Preferences. The runFullTrust capability is required for the normal Win32 desktop process, global shortcuts, per-display click-through windows and Windows Magnification full-desktop color processing. It does not request elevation, install a driver/service, inject code, capture the screen, record keys or access the secure desktop. The StartupTask is disabled by default and only enabled through an explicit user preference. Saved-dimming resume is a separate opt-in. Emergency restore: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12. Select All displays and adjust the slider for uniform desktop color processing. Per-display differences or an unavailable/busy color API use compatibility overlays. Quit from the tray menu to restore the desktop. Windows 11 desktop target; x64 and ARM64 builds. Alpha 2 adds an opt-in Desktops page. Detection reads local Explorer virtual desktop IDs/names with registry notifications and public desktop-manager fallback; it does not create desktops, use private shell interfaces or transmit metadata. Unavailable detection falls back to shared brightness. Startup/resume remain separate opt-ins.
